---
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Statement leaf template. Copy this whole folder (index.qmd, latex/, pdf/,
# lean/, sessions/) to c/<next-id>/ to start a new statement. See /schema/
# for the full frontmatter contract and CONTRIBUTING.md for the identifier
# allocation and revision rules.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Next sequential id, zero-padded to four digits. Allocated once, never
# reused -- if this statement is later withdrawn, the id stays with a
# tombstone page, it does not go back into a pool.
id: "0000"

# Exactly one hub slug (a directory under p/). A statement belongs to one
# problem; it can still belong to several areas below.
problem: example-problem-slug

title: "Precise, fully-quantified title of the statement"

# Short enough to fit a listing-table column; falls back to title if omitted.
short_title: "Short form for tables"

# Tag list, display only (not a home directory). First entry is primary.
# Must be a subset of the 19 fixed area slugs -- see AREA_SLUGS in
# scripts/build_index.py. Keep the existing 19 names; do not rename here.
areas: [idealized-models]

# One of: rom | prom | icm | ggm | qrom | standard | other
model: standard

# One of: separation | lower-bound | tight-bound | equivalence |
#         impossibility | assumption | characterization
form: lower-bound

# One of: unconditional | falsifiable | non-falsifiable
assumption_class: unconditional

# One of: research-open | research-solved | test | api | withdrawn
# research-solved and test are for solved special cases and sanity lemmas --
# they belong on the site too, not just open problems.
category: research-open

# Hash of the '## Statement' tab content below, script-maintained by
# scripts/status_badge.py. Leave any placeholder value here; the script
# fills it in on first run and rewrites it (forcing statement_match back to
# open, bumping revision) whenever the statement text changes underneath it.
statement_sha: "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"

# Bumped by scripts/status_badge.py when statement_sha changes. A change to
# wording/notation/exposition only bumps revision on the SAME id; a change
# to truth conditions (added hypothesis, changed quantifier order, different
# parameter regime) means a NEW id instead, with this one superseded-by it.
revision: 1

# The existing six fields, unchanged in meaning or grading. See
# scripts/status_badge.py and /open-problems/status-legend/.
status:
  statement_informal: ai
  statement_formal: open
  statement_match: open
  proof_informal: open
  proof_review: ai
  proof_formal: open

# Generated by scripts/status_badge.py. Never hand-edit.
status_badge: "<generated, never hand-edited>"

# One required sentence, rendered next to the badge in listing tables so a
# facet page is scannable without opening every leaf.
status_summary: "One-sentence summary of where this statement actually stands."

status_updated: 2026-01-01

# Closed vocabulary: generalizes, specializes, implies, implied-by,
# equivalent-to, strengthens, variant-of, refutes, refuted-by, superseded-by.
# Optional 'note' field required on equivalent-to edges whose proof grades
# (pi) disagree -- scripts/check_relations.py enforces this.
relations: []
  # - {kind: specializes, target: "0000"}
  # - {kind: variant-of,  target: "0000", note: "which axis differs"}

lean:
  # One of: in-repo | external-lean4 | other-system | none
  mode: none
  # repo: "https://github.com/..."       # only for external-lean4
  # commit: "..."                        # required once statement_formal != open, for external-lean4
  # path: "..."                          # path to the .lean file, either mode
  # decl: "..."                          # the Lean declaration name
  # toolchain: "leanprover/lean4:v4.x.y"

# Real citations only -- never write a specific author/venue/year citation
# here without having verified it exists. Leave the list empty rather than
# invent one.
sources: []
  # - {cite: "Author, Year, Venue, Theorem N", url: "https://..."}

# Only present when category: withdrawn. Free text explaining why, paired
# with a {kind: superseded-by, target: ...} relation above. A withdrawn
# statement's page stays up as a tombstone -- never delete it, never let its
# id 404.
# withdrawn_reason: ""
---

<!-- status:start -->
<!-- regenerated by scripts/status_badge.py -- do not hand-edit between these markers -->
<!-- status:end -->

## Status

{status_summary}. Expand here with free prose: what's been tried, what's
known for special cases, where the argument is stuck, which lemma is
load-bearing, what a resolution would imply. No length cap and nothing here
is truncated -- this is what the badge summarizes but can't say.

### Open obligations

- [ ] Replace this with the actual outstanding items: unverified steps,
      unaudited files, unmatched formalizations, missing sanity lemmas.

## Sessions

Dumps of prompt/agent sessions attempting this statement are kept in
`sessions/` for provenance. They are not rendered as part of the site.

## Changelog

- **Revision 1** (2026-01-01): initial statement.

## Statement

[View PDF](pdf/main.pdf) · [Download LaTeX source](latex/main.tex)

State the statement precisely here, using standard math notation. This
section (from this heading to the next) is exactly what `statement_sha`
hashes -- editing it without an accompanying reason is what trips the
integrity check.

## Proof

This statement is open -- no proof exists yet.

Once (an attempt at) a proof exists, add its own `.tex` source and compiled
PDF (e.g. `latex/proof.tex` / `pdf/proof.pdf`) and link them here.

## Formal Artifact

[Lean statement](lean/Statement.lean) -- autoformalized by ⟨name the AI model
here⟩. Once a human has checked it against the statement above, raise
`status.statement_match` to `human` (or `ai` if an AI checked the match).

Only the statement has been formalized so far (as a Lean theorem ending in
`sorry`), not a proof. Once a proof exists, set `status.proof_informal` /
`status.proof_review` / `status.proof_formal` accordingly and regenerate the
badge with `scripts/status_badge.py`.

:::
